about: Ten reconciliation scenarios, each built alone: open subscriptions (receipts) waiting for money, and deposit lines on a client money statement as the narration reader would leave them (remitter and reference). A receipt's reference is ATR- plus the first eight characters of its instruction id, so the builder gives each instruction an id that starts with its code. The truth is what a careful operations analyst would match; decoys are lines that must never be proposed. The rules match an exact reference with the exact amount, or a line without a reference paid by the holder whose amount exactly one receipt and one line share; the scorer adds 0.6 for the reference (less 0.15 a character away, up to two), 0.3 for the exact amount (0.15 within $1) and up to 0.1 for the payer's name, and proposes at 0.7 or more, or two or three lines from one payer that add up to one receipt.

cases.why: The line quotes ATR-4471AB2C, Ava Thompson's reference, and pays exactly the $1,500.00 owed: the rules match it.

lines.description: ACH CREDIT AVA THOMPSON REF ATR-4471AB2C

cases.why: No reference, but Lucas Moreau paid $2,500.00, the only receipt and the only line for that amount, and the payer is the holder: the rules match it.
The line quotes ATR-7F3K200D for Hana Sato's ATR-7F3K201D, one character away, with the exact $3,000.00 and the holder's name: a fuzzy match the rules leave to the scorer (0.45 + 0.3 + 0.1 = 0.85).

lines.description: ACH CREDIT HANA SATO REF ATR-7F3K200D

cases.why: Two receipts of $500.00 and two lines of $500.00 without references; each payer is one of the holders, so Priya Raman's line pays Priya Raman's receipt and Tom Becker's pays Tom Becker's. The amount alone is not unique, so the rules cannot match, and the scorer's 0.4 is under its bar; this is the agent's work.
Sofia Rossi owes $1,250.00 and paid $787.50 and $462.50, PART 1 OF 2 and PART 2 OF 2, which add up to it exactly: the two lines together pay the one receipt.

lines.description: ACH CREDIT SOFIA ROSSI PART 1 OF 2
ACH CREDIT SOFIA ROSSI PART 2 OF 2

cases.why: Kenji Watanabe owes $2,000.00 and $1,000.00 on two subscriptions and paid $3,000.00 in one wire: the one line pays both receipts. Proposals pair lines with one receipt, so no part of Atrium can propose this yet; the case records the miss in recall.
cases.known_gap: A proposal pairs lines with one subscription, so one deposit for two subscriptions cannot be proposed: the pair is shown but left out of recall.

cases.why: The bank's INTEREST PAID credit happens to be $500.00, the amount Olivia Brooks owes, but interest has no payer and no reference and is not a client's payment: it must not be matched.
Kestrel Trading Ltd wired $2,750.00 quoting an invoice, not an Atrium reference; no receipt is for that amount or that payer: nothing should be matched.

lines.description: WIRE IN KESTREL TRADING LTD REF INV 2231

cases.why: Arjun Mehta's line quotes the exact reference ATR-7V6U5T4S with the holder's name but is $0.50 short of the $800.00 owed, a bank fee taken on the way: the right match, but not exact, so the scorer proposes it (0.6 + 0.15 + 0.1 = 0.85).

lines.description: ACH CREDIT ARJUN MEHTA REF ATR-7V6U5T4S

cases.why: The narration writes Noah Williams's reference as REF ATR 4471 CD9E, with spaces, so the rule reading finds no reference on the line; two receipts wait for $1,200.00, so the amount cannot tell them apart. The narration still names Noah Williams and the code 4471CD9E: the line pays Noah Williams's receipt.
